audit_findings.title: Unreserved Brazil tax exposure is a senior claim on equity
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $120 million, equal to $2.95 per share and 12.0% of $996 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An expected present-value liability would be deducted in the equity bridge because historical OE contains no loss provision.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the terms of the Tax Matters Agreement, International Paper will pay 60 %, and Sylvamo will pay 40 % on up to $ 300 million of any assessment related to this matter, and International Paper will pay all amounts of the assessment over $ 300 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual exposure is demonstrated, although an adverse outcome and payment timing remain uncertain. The maximum claim is large relative to the modeled equity values and therefore is reasonably capable of materially reducing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain counsel's outcome probabilities, expected settlement timing and tax deductibility; calculate the present value of Sylvamo's share and rerun every scenario with that bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores the scheduled Riverdale exit
audit_findings.magnitude: 350,000 short tons of annual offtake capacity; the filed combined Riverdale/Eastover transition impact is $85 million of unfavorable 2026 Adjusted EBITDA
audit_findings.mechanism: The exit changes the earnings perimeter underlying the FY2025 OE anchor and affects near-term OE and the defensibility of positive growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: In October 2025, we agreed with International Paper that supply under the offtake agreement will wind down after April 30, 2026 and terminate on May 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter omission, not merely a possible future risk: Riverdale supply terminated in 2026, while the model carries FY2025 OE forward without an adjustment. The $85 million filed transition impact exceeds the $62.1 million OE anchor, although the portion attributable solely to Riverdale and the enduring effect remain unquantified. Eastover's filed $50 million expected annual EBITDA benefit may later offset part of the loss but does not repair the missing reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to post-Riverdale recurring OE, separately identifying lost contribution, displaced or replaced volume, transition costs, Eastover constraints, required investment and the timing of the filed Eastover benefits; rerun the valuation from the reconciled perimeter.

audit_findings.title: A LIFO liquidation benefit may remain in normalized earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $12 million pretax, equal to 19.3% of the $62.1 million OE anchor; after-tax amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the nonrecurring inventory-layer benefit inflates the OE anchor and therefore projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The effect of this liquidation was to increase income before income taxes in the North America segment by approximately $ 12 million and $ 12 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The $12 million 2025 pretax benefit is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether the OE calculation already removed it or how much entered OE after tax and working-capital treatment. Its scale relative to the anchor makes the issue potentially material, but materiality cannot be established until the OE reconciliation is inspected.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $12 million benefit through net income, taxes and working-capital adjustments into 2025 OE; if present, remove the nonrecurring after-tax amount and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Target PSUs do not establish a true dilution ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 520,058 PSUs at target, equal to 1.28% of the 40.744942 million-share denominator; incremental above-target dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Maximum vesting would increase fully diluted shares and reduce value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The following sets forth restricted stock units and performance-based restricted stock units at 100% of target amounts at December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023:
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that PSU disclosure is at target, but it does not supply the maximum payout multiplier or establish how the valuation denominator treated subsequent awards and settlements. Target PSUs alone are modest relative to the denominator, but no supported upper bound exists for incremental dilution, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain award-level maximum payout multipliers and reconcile maximum vesting, 2026 grants, settlements, forfeitures and dividend-equivalent treatment through the valuation date; rerun per-share values using the resulting no-offset share ceiling.

audit_findings.title: The unreserved Brazilian VAT assessment is another senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $57 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.40 per share and 5.7% of $996 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A loss would be deducted from the equity bridge because no reserve or historical OE charge captures it.
audit_findings.evidence: During the first quarter of 2024, the State of Sao Paulo issued a tax assessment to Sylvamo Brasil for approximately $ 51 million (adjusted for variation in currency exchange rates) regarding unpaid VAT arising from intercompany transactions.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed exposure is $57 million rather than the earlier $51 million. Even deducting the entire undiscounted assessment would reduce modeled values to approximately $16.96 bear, $23.03 base and $25.53 bull per share; the bull value would remain $10.44 below the $35.97 market price. Accordingly, this claim does not change the existing valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers, although it reduces value.
audit_findings.action: Continue tracking litigation, currency, interest and penalties; rerun the bridge if the assessment grows materially, loss probability changes, or a payment or reserve becomes probable.

audit_findings.title: U.K. pension amendments could create unrecorded backdated obligations
audit_findings.mechanism: Any incremental pension liability would reduce the equity bridge, while required contributions could also reduce future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Any such outcome could result in a material increase in our U.K. pension plan liabilities and require increased contributions or additional funding.
audit_findings.explanation: The legal uncertainty relates to historical amendments and therefore is a present contingent exposure, not merely a forward-looking operating risk. Reported company-wide pension assets of $338 million and obligations of $340 million do not measure the possible backdated U.K. benefits. Without an actuary's affected-benefit estimate, the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain counsel's assessment of which amendments lack valid documentation and an actuarial range for backdated benefits, tax effects, timing and funding requirements; deduct the present-value liability or model the resulting contributions and rerun if material.
